name: 500 (Sicilian)
description: 500 Sicilian is a variant of the trick-taking game 500 adapted for the 40-card Sicilian/Italian deck (Coins, Cups, Swords, Clubs; 1-7 + Fante/Cavallo/Re). Bidding for tricks + trump suit. Misère available. Adapted scoring and hand structure for 40-card deck. First to 500 points wins. Kitty/widow for bid winner.

history.origins: 500 (Five Hundred) originated in the United States as an extension of Euchre, developed before 1900 and copyrighted by the US Playing Card Company in 1904. It became the national card game of Australia and spread to New Zealand, Canada, and elsewhere. Sicilian 500 is a regional adaptation: Italian and Sicilian players later adapted 500's bidding and trick-taking structure to the 40-card Italian deck used in local games such as Briscola and Scopa, preserving contract bidding, kitty, and first-to-500 scoring while using Italian suits and face cards (Fante, Cavallo, Re).
timeline: Early 20th century: 500 spreads from American and Australian play and is documented as a popular bidding game in English-language sources.
Later 20th century: Sicilian and Italian players adapt 500’s bidding and trick structure to the 40-card Italian deck used in local games such as Briscola and Scopa.
history.evolution: Merges American bidding game with Italian deck tradition.

setup.deck: 40 Sicilian cards: 4 suits (Coins/Cups/Swords/Clubs), 1-7 + Fante + Cavallo + Re.

rules.objective: Reach 500 points first by making and fulfilling bids. Bid for number of tricks and trump (or Misère); bid winner takes the kitty, discards, and must make the contract to score; opponents score tricks they take.
rules.gameplay: Bid for tricks + trump. Winner takes kitty, discards. Follow suit, trump if void. Misère = lose all tricks. Make contract: score bid value. Fail: lose bid value. Non-bidders score tricks won.

variations.name: Misère
variations.description: Bid to lose every trick; no trump. Contract: take zero tricks; fail scores negative.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Misère is described in rules text as a bid to lose every trick; no separate engine override fields have been modeled for it yet.

scoring.description: Contract-based. Bid value scored if contract made; failed bid scores negative. Opponents score tricks. First to 500 wins.
